zones.name: Brain & sleep
zones.blurb: Peptides that act on the nervous system: cognition, mood, pain signalling, sleep and neurodevelopment.

zones.name: Skin & aging
zones.blurb: Topicals, pigment-acting peptides and the antibiotics that treat skin infections.

zones.name: Digestive & weight
zones.blurb: Gut hormones, incretins and the peptides behind modern weight-loss and GI medicine.

zones.name: Hormones & metabolism
zones.blurb: Insulin, growth hormone, pituitary and adrenal signalling, and mitochondrial peptides.

zones.name: Bones & muscles
zones.blurb: Bone builders, growth-hormone secretagogues and tissue-repair peptides.

zones.name: Heart & blood
zones.blurb: Blood pressure, clotting, blood cells and the vascular system.

zones.name: Sexual & reproductive
zones.blurb: Fertility, reproductive hormones, hormone-driven cancers and libido.

peptides.name: Bremelanotide
peptides.route: As-needed injection under the skin with a single-use autoinjector
peptides.status: FDA-approved in 2019 for low sexual desire (HSDD) in premenopausal women
peptides.mechanism: Activates melanocortin receptors, mainly MC4R, in brain circuits linked to sexual desire, rather than acting on genital blood flow
uses: Hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women
peptides.summary: Bremelanotide (Vyleesi) is an as-needed injection approved in 2019 for premenopausal women with distressing low sexual desire. It acts on brain pathways, not blood flow.

peptides.name: Trofinetide
peptides.route: Liquid taken twice daily by mouth or through a feeding tube
peptides.status: FDA-approved in March 2023 for Rett syndrome in people 2 years and older; authorized in the EU in 2026
peptides.mechanism: Mimics GPE, a three-amino-acid fragment of IGF-1 made in the brain, which may ease brain inflammation and support synapses; its exact action is unknown
uses: Rett syndrome (adults and children 2 years and older)
peptides.summary: Trofinetide (Daybue) is a twice-daily oral drug approved in 2023 as the first treatment for Rett syndrome. It is a modified fragment of IGF-1, and diarrhea is very common.

peptides.name: Ziconotide
peptides.route: Slow continuous infusion into the spinal fluid through an implanted pump
peptides.status: FDA-approved in 2004 for severe chronic pain when other treatments fail or are not tolerated
peptides.mechanism: Blocks N-type calcium channels on pain nerve endings in the spinal cord, so they release less of the chemicals that relay pain to the brain
uses: Severe chronic pain not controlled by other treatments
peptides.summary: Ziconotide (Prialt) is a synthetic cone-snail toxin infused into the spinal fluid for severe chronic pain. It is not an opioid but has serious psychiatric warnings.

peptides.name: Davunetide
peptides.route: Nasal spray (in clinical trials)
peptides.status: Investigational; failed a phase 2/3 trial in progressive supranuclear palsy; now being pursued for ADNP syndrome
peptides.mechanism: An eight-amino-acid piece of the brain protein ADNP that interacts with microtubule-tracking proteins, supporting the nerve cell skeleton and tau
peptides.summary: Davunetide (NAP) is an experimental nasal-spray peptide from the brain protein ADNP. It failed in progressive supranuclear palsy and is now aimed at ADNP syndrome.

peptides.name: NNZ-2591
peptides.cls: Cyclic dipeptide analog of an IGF-1 metabolite
peptides.route: Oral liquid taken twice daily (in trials)
peptides.status: Investigational; phase 3 trial in Phelan-McDermid syndrome under way since late 2025; not FDA-approved
peptides.mechanism: Mimics cyclic glycine-proline, a small IGF-1 breakdown product thought to keep IGF-1 activity in the brain within a healthy range
peptides.summary: NNZ-2591 is an oral, experimental IGF-1-related drug from the makers of trofinetide, now in a phase 3 trial for Phelan-McDermid syndrome. It is not approved.

peptides.name: Trofinetide (investigational uses)
peptides.route: Tested as an IV infusion (brain injury) and as an oral liquid (fragile X)
peptides.status: Approved only for Rett syndrome (Daybue); brain injury, concussion and fragile X programs stalled, with no active trials
peptides.mechanism: A stabilized copy of GPE, an IGF-1 fragment that limited inflammation and nerve-cell death after brain injury in animal studies
peptides.summary: Before trofinetide was approved for Rett syndrome, it was tested for brain injury, concussion and fragile X syndrome. Those programs stalled, and none is active in 2026.

peptides.name: Epitalon
peptides.route: Usually injected under the skin (unapproved products)
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA advisers backed allowing compounding in July 2026, but the FDA has not acted on that vote
peptides.mechanism: Proposed to switch on telomerase and influence melatonin and gene activity, based mainly on cell and animal studies
peptides.summary: Epitalon is a four-amino-acid peptide from Russian aging research, sold for longevity and sleep. Evidence comes mostly from cells and animals, and it is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Semax
peptides.route: Nasal drops or spray (unapproved products in the US)
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA advisers backed allowing compounding in July 2026, but no final FDA action yet; approved in Russia
peptides.mechanism: A stabilized fragment of the stress hormone ACTH, without its hormonal effect, that raises the brain growth factor BDNF in animal studies
peptides.summary: Semax is a nasal peptide developed in Russia for stroke and cognition and sold online as a nootropic. It is not FDA-approved, and Western clinical trials are lacking.

peptides.name: Selank
peptides.route: Nasal drops or spray; sometimes injected (unapproved products in the US)
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved and not eligible for US compounding; registered as an anxiety drug in Russia
peptides.mechanism: A stabilized version of the immune peptide tuftsin that, in Russian studies, slows enkephalin breakdown and shifts GABA-related gene activity
peptides.summary: Selank is a Russian nasal peptide promoted online for anxiety and focus. Evidence comes from small Russian studies, and it is not FDA-approved or legally compounded in the US.

peptides.name: PT-141
peptides.route: Injected under the skin or sprayed in the nose (unapproved products)
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved as sold online or as PT-141; the same molecule is approved as Vyleesi for HSDD in premenopausal women
peptides.mechanism: Activates brain melanocortin receptors, mainly MC4R, that influence sexual desire and erections; chemically identical to approved bremelanotide
peptides.summary: PT-141 is the research name for bremelanotide, sold online and by some clinics for libido. Only the Vyleesi injection is FDA-approved, and only for premenopausal women.

peptides.name: DSIP
peptides.route: Usually injected under the skin (unapproved products)
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA advisers voted against allowing compounding in July 2026
peptides.mechanism: Unclear; first reported to promote deep slow-wave sleep in rabbits, but no gene, precursor or receptor for it has been found
peptides.summary: DSIP is a nine-amino-acid peptide discovered in 1977 and sold online for sleep. Its role in sleep was never confirmed, human trials were weak, and it is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Dihexa
peptides.route: Taken by mouth, applied to skin or injected (unapproved products)
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; never tested in human trials; not eligible for US compounding
peptides.mechanism: Claimed to boost hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) signaling through its receptor c-Met to grow new synapses, though a key study was retracted
peptides.summary: Dihexa is a lab-made angiotensin IV analog sold online as a memory booster. It has never been tested in people, a key study was retracted, and it is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Cerebrolysin
peptides.route: Injection or IV infusion where it is licensed (not available in the US)
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; prescribed in some other countries for stroke, dementia and brain injury
peptides.mechanism: A mixture of small peptides and amino acids from pig brain, said to act like natural nerve growth factors, though its active components are not defined
peptides.summary: Cerebrolysin is a mixture of small peptides and amino acids made from pig brain tissue and prescribed in some countries. It is not FDA-approved, and trial results are mixed and often low quality.

peptides.name: Afamelanotide
peptides.route: Small implant placed under the skin by a trained clinician every 2 months
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2019) to increase pain-free light exposure in adults with erythropoietic protoporphyria
peptides.mechanism: Copies the hormone alpha-MSH at the MC1R receptor on pigment cells, raising dark eumelanin that filters the light which triggers EPP pain
peptides.summary: Afamelanotide (Scenesse) is a dissolving implant that darkens skin pigment so adults with erythropoietic protoporphyria can spend more time in light without pain. FDA-approved in 2019.

peptides.name: Bacitracin
peptides.route: Ointment applied to the skin 1-3 times a day; prescription eye ointments also exist
peptides.status: FDA-approved for topical use (OTC first-aid ointment); the injectable form was withdrawn for safety reasons in 2020-2022
peptides.mechanism: Ties up the lipid carrier bacteria use to move cell-wall building blocks, so susceptible Gram-positive bacteria cannot build their walls
uses: Preventing infection in minor cuts, scrapes and burns
peptides.summary: Bacitracin is a peptide antibiotic made by Bacillus bacteria, sold over the counter as a first-aid ointment for minor wounds. Its injectable form was pulled from the US market for safety.

peptides.name: Dalbavancin / Oritavancin / Telavancin
peptides.route: Intravenous infusion: one or two doses (dalbavancin, oritavancin) or daily (telavancin)
peptides.status: FDA-approved: telavancin (2009), dalbavancin and oritavancin (2014) for serious bacterial skin infections
peptides.mechanism: Block bacterial cell-wall assembly like vancomycin, while a fatty side chain anchors them to the bacterial membrane for added potency and staying power
uses: Acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections
Infections caused by MRSA and other Gram-positive bacteria
peptides.summary: Dalbavancin, oritavancin and telavancin are IV lipoglycopeptide antibiotics for serious skin infections, including MRSA. The first two can treat an infection in one or two doses.

peptides.name: Daptomycin
peptides.route: IV infusion or 2-minute IV injection, once a day (adults)
peptides.status: FDA-approved for complicated skin infections (2003) and S. aureus bloodstream infections (2006); generics available
peptides.mechanism: With calcium, inserts into Gram-positive bacterial membranes and seizes cell-wall building blocks, collapsing the membrane and killing the cell
uses: Complicated skin and skin structure infections
peptides.summary: Daptomycin (Cubicin) is a once-daily IV antibiotic for serious skin infections and Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections, including MRSA. It is not used for pneumonia.

peptides.name: Difelikefalin
peptides.route: IV injection into the dialysis line at the end of each hemodialysis session
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2021) for moderate-to-severe itch from chronic kidney disease in adults on hemodialysis
peptides.mechanism: Activates kappa-opioid receptors on nerves and immune cells outside the brain, damping itch signals without the euphoria of brain-acting opioids
uses: Itch from chronic kidney disease in adults on hemodialysis
peptides.summary: Difelikefalin (Korsuva) is an IV peptide given after hemodialysis to relieve moderate-to-severe itch caused by chronic kidney disease. FDA-approved in 2021.

peptides.name: Ecallantide
peptides.route: Three injections under the skin, given by a healthcare professional during an attack
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2009) for acute hereditary angioedema attacks in people 12 and older; boxed warning for anaphylaxis
peptides.mechanism: Blocks plasma kallikrein, the enzyme that releases bradykinin, so the fluid leak behind hereditary angioedema swelling slows and stops
peptides.summary: Ecallantide (Kalbitor) is an injected kallikrein blocker that treats sudden swelling attacks of hereditary angioedema. It is FDA-approved but must be given by a clinician because of anaphylaxis risk.

peptides.name: Icatibant
peptides.route: Self-injected under the skin of the abdomen during an attack
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2011) for acute hereditary angioedema attacks in adults; generic versions available since 2019
peptides.mechanism: Sits in the bradykinin B2 receptor without activating it, so bradykinin cannot trigger the blood-vessel leak that causes HAE swelling
uses: Acute attacks of hereditary angioedema in adults
peptides.summary: Icatibant (Firazyr and generics) is a self-injected peptide that blocks bradykinin receptors to stop swelling attacks of hereditary angioedema in adults. FDA-approved in 2011.

peptides.name: LTX-315
peptides.route: Injected directly into tumors by a clinician
peptides.status: Investigational: phase 2 trials in basal cell carcinoma, melanoma and sarcoma; not approved anywhere as of 2026
peptides.mechanism: Punctures cancer-cell and mitochondrial membranes, causing a messy cell death that releases danger signals and recruits T cells against the tumor
peptides.summary: LTX-315 is an experimental 9-amino-acid peptide injected into tumors to burst cancer cells and prime the immune system. It is in phase 2 trials, including for basal cell carcinoma.

peptides.name: GHK-Cu
peptides.route: Injected under the skin (unapproved) or applied to skin in cosmetics
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved as a drug; injectable use is unapproved and its compounding status was under FDA review as of 2026
peptides.mechanism: Carries copper into cells and appears to switch on repair programs in skin cells, raising collagen and blood-vessel growth in lab and animal studies
peptides.summary: GHK-Cu is a natural copper-binding tripeptide used in skincare and sold as an unapproved injectable for skin, hair and healing. Human evidence for injection is essentially absent.

peptides.name: Melanotan II
peptides.route: Injected under the skin or used as a nasal spray (unapproved, gray-market)
peptides.status: Not approved anywhere; never cleared by the FDA, which lists serious reported harms; under FDA advisory review for compounding in 2026-27
peptides.mechanism: Mimics alpha-MSH at several melanocortin receptors, darkening skin through MC1R and acting on brain receptors that affect appetite and sexual arousal
peptides.summary: Melanotan II is an unapproved synthetic hormone analog sold online as a tanning injection or nasal spray. It darkens skin and moles and has been linked to melanoma and other serious harms.

peptides.name: Glutathione
peptides.route: Oral supplement; also IV drips, injections, inhaled and topical forms (not FDA-approved)
peptides.status: Not an FDA-approved drug; sold as an oral dietary supplement; injectable forms are pharmacy-compounded, with FDA contamination alerts
peptides.mechanism: The body's main internal antioxidant: neutralizes reactive molecules, helps the liver tag toxins for removal, and in skin nudges pigment cells toward lighter melanin
peptides.summary: Glutathione is the body's main antioxidant tripeptide, sold as a supplement and given in IV wellness drips, often for skin lightening. Evidence is modest and IV products carry contamination risks.

peptides.name: Melanotan I
peptides.route: Gray-market injections under the skin; the approved form is a clinician-placed implant
peptides.status: Not approved for tanning; the same molecule is FDA-approved only as Scenesse (afamelanotide) for a rare light-sensitivity disease
peptides.mechanism: Copies the hormone alpha-MSH at the MC1R receptor on pigment cells, boosting dark eumelanin to produce a tan without sun exposure
peptides.summary: Melanotan I is the research name for afamelanotide, a synthetic tanning hormone. It is sold online as an unapproved injection; the only approved form is an implant for a rare disease.

peptides.name: Acetyl hexapeptide-8
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: Mimics part of the nerve protein SNAP-25 and, in lab tests, interferes with the machinery nerves use to release signals that tighten facial muscles
peptides.summary: Acetyl hexapeptide-8 (Argireline) is a skincare peptide marketed as a topical alternative to Botox for expression lines. Small studies show modest smoothing; it does not paralyze muscles.

peptides.name: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: Copies a fragment of collagen that, in cultured cells, signals connective-tissue cells to build more collagen and fibronectin
peptides.summary: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (Matrixyl) is a skincare peptide designed to stimulate collagen. One 12-week placebo-controlled trial showed fewer visible wrinkles; other evidence is limited.

peptides.name: Copper tripeptide-1
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug (injectable GHK-Cu is a separate question)
peptides.mechanism: A natural three-amino-acid peptide that binds copper and, in lab studies, nudges skin cells toward wound repair and collagen turnover
peptides.summary: Copper tripeptide-1 (GHK-Cu) is a skincare ingredient used for aging skin and post-procedure care. Human trials are few and small, and one found no objective benefit over standard care.

peptides.name: Acetyl octapeptide-3
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums, creams and microneedle patches
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: An eight-amino-acid extension of acetyl hexapeptide-8 that is meant to imitate a nerve protein and, in theory, soften signals that tighten facial muscles
peptides.summary: Acetyl octapeptide-3 (SNAP-8) is a skincare peptide marketed as a gentler alternative to Botox for expression lines. Published human data are limited to combination products.

peptides.name: Acetyl tetrapeptide-5
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in eye creams and gels
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: Proposed to ease eye-area puffiness by affecting the enzyme ACE and slowing glycation, based mainly on lab and manufacturer data
peptides.summary: Acetyl tetrapeptide-5 (Eyeseryl) is an eye-cream peptide marketed to reduce under-eye puffiness. No independent human trial of the peptide alone was found, so evidence is very limited.

peptides.name: Carnosine
peptides.route: Applied to the skin, or taken by mouth as a supplement
peptides.status: Cosmetic and dietary supplement ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: A two-amino-acid molecule found in muscle and brain that buffers acid, mops up reactive molecules and blocks glycation (sugar damage to proteins)
peptides.summary: Carnosine is a natural dipeptide used in skincare as an antioxidant and anti-glycation agent. Support comes mainly from lab and skin-sample studies, not trials of wrinkles in people.

peptides.name: Dipeptide diaminobutyroyl benzylamide diacetate
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: A small synthetic molecule designed to imitate waglerin-1, a viper venom peptide that blocks muscle acetylcholine receptors, to ease facial muscle tension
peptides.summary: Dipeptide diaminobutyroyl benzylamide diacetate (Syn-Ake) is a skincare ingredient inspired by viper venom and marketed for expression lines. Human evidence comes mainly from combination products.

peptides.name: Hexapeptide-9
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: Marketed as a signal that prompts skin cells to make collagen IV and laminin, proteins that bind the skin layers together; published support is thin
peptides.summary: Hexapeptide-9 is a cosmetic peptide marketed to firm skin by boosting collagen IV and laminin. Evidence for the standard form is thin; a 2025 trial tested a newer cyclized version instead.

peptides.name: Nonapeptide-1
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: Designed to compete with the hormone alpha-MSH at the melanocortin 1 receptor on pigment cells, which in theory lowers melanin production
peptides.summary: Nonapeptide-1 is a cosmetic peptide marketed for brightening dark spots by blocking a pigment-signaling receptor. Human data come from combination products, so evidence is very limited.

peptides.name: Oligopeptide-1
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: Mimics epidermal growth factor, a signal that tells skin cells to divide and repair; whether cosmetic versions match the real protein is debated
uses: Texture and firmness of photoaged skin
peptides.summary: Oligopeptide-1 is the cosmetic name for recombinant epidermal growth factor (EGF) used in skin-renewal serums. Wound-care trials support EGF drugs; evidence for cosmetic versions is small and disputed.

peptides.name: Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: Copies a repeating piece of elastin that, in cell studies, stimulates skin fibroblasts; benefit for wrinkles in people is unproven
peptides.summary: Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12 is a skincare peptide modeled on a fragment of elastin, marketed for firmness and elasticity. Evidence is mainly cell and skin-sample work, with no large human trial found.

peptides.name: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: Proposed to dampen inflammation signals such as interleukin-6 so skin shows less age and sun damage; human proof is lacking
peptides.summary: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 is a skincare peptide marketed to calm inflammation and smooth lines, usually paired with palmitoyl tripeptide-1. Human evidence for it alone is lacking.

peptides.name: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: A fatty-acid-modified version of the natural peptide GHK, proposed to prompt skin cells to make collagen and other matrix proteins
peptides.summary: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 (Pal-GHK) is a fatty-acid-modified skincare peptide marketed to boost collagen, often paired with palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7. A 2025 review found surprisingly few clinical studies.

peptides.name: Palmitoyl tripeptide-38
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: Marketed to boost six components of the skin's supporting matrix; support is mainly open-label, combination-product data
peptides.summary: Palmitoyl tripeptide-38 (Matrixyl synthe'6) is a skincare peptide marketed to reduce wrinkles. Published human data are open-label studies of multi-ingredient products, so evidence is very limited.

peptides.name: Pentapeptide-18
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: An enkephalin-like peptide proposed to calm the nerve signals that tighten facial muscles and so ease expression lines; shown mainly in lab settings
peptides.summary: Pentapeptide-18 (Leuphasyl) is a skincare peptide marketed to relax expression lines by calming nerve signals. Published work is mostly lab characterization and formulation studies, not clinical trials.

peptides.name: Tripeptide-10 citrulline
peptides.route: Applied to the skin in serums and creams
peptides.status: Cosmetic ingredient; not an FDA-approved drug
peptides.mechanism: A lab-designed peptide that imitates decorin, a protein that keeps collagen fibers thin and evenly spaced; shown in test-tube assays only
peptides.summary: Tripeptide-10 citrulline is a skincare peptide designed to act like decorin and tidy collagen fibers. The main paper uses test-tube assays; human evidence is lacking.

peptides.name: Semaglutide
peptides.route: Weekly injection under the skin, or a daily tablet
peptides.status: FDA-approved: type 2 diabetes (2017), weight management (2021), heart, kidney and liver indications since
peptides.mechanism: Mimics the gut hormone GLP-1 to release insulin when blood sugar is high, slow stomach emptying and quiet appetite signals in the brain
uses: Cutting heart attack and stroke risk
peptides.summary: Semaglutide is a once-weekly GLP-1 drug (Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus) approved for type 2 diabetes and weight loss, with proven heart and kidney benefits.

peptides.name: Tirzepatide
peptides.cls: Dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist
peptides.route: Weekly injection under the skin, from a pen or vial
peptides.status: FDA-approved: type 2 diabetes (2022), weight management (2023), sleep apnea (2024), heart risk in diabetes (2026)
peptides.mechanism: Switches on receptors for two gut hormones, GIP and GLP-1, to boost insulin when glucose is high, slow digestion and quiet appetite
uses: Heart attack and stroke risk in type 2 diabetes
peptides.summary: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) is a once-weekly injection that acts on two gut-hormone receptors. It is FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes, weight management and sleep apnea.

peptides.name: Dasiglucagon
peptides.route: Single-dose injection under the skin (autoinjector or prefilled syringe)
peptides.status: FDA-approved in 2021 for severe low blood sugar in people with diabetes aged 6 and older
peptides.mechanism: A stabilized copy of glucagon that tells the liver to release stored glucose, rapidly raising dangerously low blood sugar
peptides.summary: Dasiglucagon (Zegalogue) is a ready-to-use glucagon analog in an autoinjector, FDA-approved since 2021 to rescue severe low blood sugar in people with diabetes aged 6 and up.

peptides.name: Ga-68 dotatate
peptides.route: Single IV injection, followed by a PET scan 40-90 minutes later
peptides.status: FDA-approved in 2016 (NETSPOT kit) to locate somatostatin receptor-positive neuroendocrine tumors
peptides.mechanism: A somatostatin look-alike tagged with radioactive gallium-68 that latches onto tumor cells rich in somatostatin receptors, making them glow on a PET scan
peptides.summary: Ga-68 dotatate (NETSPOT) is a radioactive peptide tracer used with PET scans to find neuroendocrine tumors. It was FDA-approved in 2016 for adults and children.

peptides.name: Glucagon
peptides.route: Injection (under the skin, into muscle or IV) or a one-puff nasal powder
peptides.status: FDA-approved since 1960; nasal powder and ready-to-use injection versions approved in 2019
peptides.mechanism: Activates glucagon receptors in the liver to release stored glucose and raise blood sugar within minutes; it also briefly relaxes the gut wall
uses: Relaxing the gut during radiology exams
peptides.summary: Glucagon is the pancreatic hormone that raises blood sugar. FDA-approved forms, including Baqsimi nasal powder and Gvoke injections, treat severe hypoglycemia in diabetes.

peptides.name: Lanreotide
peptides.route: Deep injection under the skin of the buttock every 4 weeks
peptides.status: FDA-approved: acromegaly (2007), neuroendocrine tumors (2014), carcinoid syndrome (2017)
peptides.mechanism: Mimics somatostatin, the body's hormone brake, to hold back growth hormone and gut hormones and slow the growth of neuroendocrine tumors
peptides.summary: Lanreotide (Somatuline Depot) is a monthly somatostatin analog injection, FDA-approved for acromegaly, gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors and carcinoid syndrome.

peptides.name: Linaclotide
peptides.route: Capsule by mouth once a day, on an empty stomach
peptides.status: FDA-approved in 2012 for IBS-C and chronic constipation in adults; pediatric uses added since 2023
peptides.mechanism: Activates the guanylate cyclase-C receptor on the gut lining, drawing water into the bowel to soften stool and calming pain-sensing nerves
uses: Functional constipation in children 2 and older
peptides.summary: Linaclotide (Linzess) is a daily capsule that adds fluid to the bowel. It is FDA-approved for IBS with constipation, chronic idiopathic constipation and childhood functional constipation.

peptides.name: Liraglutide
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin with a pen
peptides.status: FDA-approved: type 2 diabetes (2010) and weight management (2014); generic versions now available
peptides.mechanism: Mimics the gut hormone GLP-1 to release insulin when blood sugar is high, slow stomach emptying and reduce appetite
uses: Type 2 diabetes in adults and children 10 and older
Lowering heart risk in type 2 diabetes with heart disease
peptides.summary: Liraglutide (Victoza, Saxenda) is a once-daily GLP-1 injection, FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes and for weight management in adults and teens. Generic versions are available.

peptides.name: Lutetium Lu-177 dotatate
peptides.route: IV infusion every 8 weeks for 4 doses, in a nuclear medicine unit
peptides.status: FDA-approved in 2018 for somatostatin receptor-positive GEP-NETs; extended to children 12 and older in 2024
peptides.mechanism: A somatostatin look-alike that carries radioactive lutetium-177 into neuroendocrine tumor cells, where its radiation damages their DNA
peptides.summary: Lutetium Lu-177 dotatate (Lutathera) is a radioactive peptide drug that targets neuroendocrine tumors. FDA-approved in 2018, it is given as four IV infusions eight weeks apart.

peptides.name: Octreotide
peptides.route: Injection under the skin or IV, monthly muscle depot, or twice-daily capsules
peptides.status: FDA-approved since 1988 for acromegaly and hormone-driven diarrhea from carcinoid tumors and VIPomas
peptides.mechanism: Mimics somatostatin to block release of growth hormone, insulin, glucagon, serotonin and other gut hormones, and reduces blood flow to the gut
peptides.summary: Octreotide (Sandostatin, Mycapssa) is a somatostatin analog used for acromegaly and hormone-secreting gut tumors, available as short-acting shots, monthly depots and oral capsules.

peptides.name: Plecanatide
peptides.route: One 3 mg tablet by mouth daily, with or without food
peptides.status: FDA-approved for adults: chronic idiopathic constipation (2017) and IBS with constipation (2018)
peptides.mechanism: Copies the gut hormone uroguanylin to switch on guanylate cyclase-C receptors in the small intestine, which pulls water into the bowel and softens stool
uses: Irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adults
peptides.summary: Plecanatide (Trulance) is a once-daily tablet that mimics the gut hormone uroguanylin. It is FDA-approved for chronic idiopathic constipation and IBS with constipation in adults.

peptides.name: Setmelanotide
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin
peptides.status: FDA-approved for rare genetic obesity (2020), Bardet-Biedl syndrome (2022) and acquired hypothalamic obesity (2026)
peptides.mechanism: Activates the melanocortin-4 receptor in the hypothalamus, restoring a fullness signal that is broken in certain genetic and brain-injury forms of obesity
uses: Obesity from POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency
peptides.summary: Setmelanotide (Imcivree) is a daily injection that restores a brain fullness signal. It is FDA-approved for rare genetic obesity, Bardet-Biedl syndrome and acquired hypothalamic obesity.

peptides.name: Sincalide
peptides.route: IV injection or slow IV infusion during a diagnostic test
peptides.status: FDA-approved diagnostic agent (Kinevac, first approved 1976); generic versions available
peptides.mechanism: Copies the active end of the gut hormone cholecystokinin, making the gallbladder squeeze, the pancreas secrete enzymes and the small bowel speed up
uses: Collecting bile or pancreatic fluid for analysis
Speeding barium through the small bowel
peptides.summary: Sincalide (Kinevac) is a synthetic piece of the gut hormone cholecystokinin, given IV during diagnostic tests to make the gallbladder contract and the pancreas secrete.

peptides.name: Teduglutide
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin, dosed by body weight
peptides.status: FDA-approved for short bowel syndrome in adults (2012) and children 1 year and older (2019)
peptides.mechanism: Mimics GLP-2, a gut hormone that thickens the intestinal lining and boosts absorption, so a shortened bowel can take in more fluid and nutrients
uses: Short bowel syndrome dependent on IV nutrition or fluids
peptides.summary: Teduglutide (Gattex) is a daily GLP-2 injection that helps the remaining bowel absorb more in short bowel syndrome, cutting the need for IV nutrition. FDA-approved since 2012.

peptides.name: Terlipressin
peptides.route: IV injection every 6 hours in the hospital, for up to 14 days
peptides.status: FDA-approved in 2022 for hepatorenal syndrome with rapidly worsening kidney function
peptides.mechanism: A long-acting vasopressin prodrug that tightens blood vessels in the gut, shifting blood back into circulation and restoring flow to the kidneys
uses: Hepatorenal syndrome in adults with cirrhosis
peptides.summary: Terlipressin (Terlivaz) is a hospital IV drug that improves kidney function in hepatorenal syndrome, a kidney failure caused by advanced liver disease. FDA-approved in 2022.

peptides.name: Tesamorelin
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin of the abdomen
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2010) to reduce excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy; not for weight loss
peptides.mechanism: Mimics growth hormone-releasing hormone so the pituitary gland releases more of its own growth hormone, which shrinks fat stored deep in the abdomen
uses: Excess belly fat in HIV-associated lipodystrophy
peptides.summary: Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is an FDA-approved daily injection that reduces deep belly fat in adults with HIV lipodystrophy. It is not for weight loss, and any use outside that group is off-label.

peptides.name: Retatrutide
peptides.route: Once-weekly injection under the skin in trials
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. Phase 3 results reported in 2026; Lilly plans to submit to the FDA in early 2027
peptides.mechanism: Activates three hormone receptors at once (GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon) to lower appetite and may also increase energy use
peptides.summary: Retatrutide is an investigational once-weekly injection from Eli Lilly that targets three hormone receptors. Phase 3 trials showed up to about 25% weight loss, but it is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Cagrilintide
peptides.route: Once-weekly injection under the skin in trials
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. Phase 3 trials are under way; a semaglutide combination (CagriSema) is under FDA review
peptides.mechanism: Copies amylin, a pancreatic hormone released with insulin that signals fullness to the brain, in a form that lasts long enough for weekly dosing
peptides.summary: Cagrilintide is an investigational once-weekly amylin analog from Novo Nordisk that lowers appetite. It is being tested alone and with semaglutide as CagriSema, and is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Amycretin
peptides.route: Once-weekly injection or daily tablet in trials
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. Phase 3 trials began in 2026 under the new name zenagamtide
peptides.mechanism: One molecule that switches on both the GLP-1 and amylin receptors to lower appetite and increase fullness
peptides.summary: Amycretin, now named zenagamtide, is an experimental Novo Nordisk drug that activates GLP-1 and amylin receptors in one molecule, as a weekly injection or daily tablet. It is in phase 3 and not approved.

peptides.name: Apraglutide
peptides.route: Once-weekly injection under the skin in trials
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. A second, confirmatory phase 3 trial for US approval began recruiting in 2026
peptides.mechanism: Long-acting copy of GLP-2, a gut hormone that helps the small intestine grow and absorb more fluid and nutrients
uses: Short bowel syndrome with intestinal failure
peptides.summary: Apraglutide is an investigational once-weekly GLP-2 injection for short bowel syndrome with intestinal failure. A phase 3 trial showed less need for IV nutrition, but a second trial is needed for US approval.

peptides.name: Brilacidin
peptides.route: Studied as an IV dose, a mouth rinse and a colon-release tablet
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. Most advanced trials are small phase 2 studies; no phase 3 trial is registered
peptides.mechanism: A small synthetic molecule that mimics defensins, natural infection-fighting proteins, to disrupt microbes and calm inflammation
peptides.summary: Brilacidin is an experimental synthetic mimic of the body's defensin proteins, studied for skin infections, radiation mouth sores and bowel inflammation. Human data are small and it is not approved.

peptides.name: CagriSema
peptides.route: Once-weekly injection under the skin in trials
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved as of this writing. Submitted in December 2025 for weight management; decision anticipated by late 2026
peptides.mechanism: Combines semaglutide (a GLP-1 drug) and cagrilintide (an amylin analog) in one weekly injection to lower appetite through two pathways
peptides.summary: CagriSema is a once-weekly injection combining semaglutide and the amylin analog cagrilintide. Phase 3 trials showed about 20% weight loss, and Novo Nordisk has asked the FDA to approve it for weight management.

peptides.name: Enlicitide
peptides.route: One tablet by mouth daily, on an empty stomach
peptides.status: FDA-approved in July 2026 (Lipfendra) to lower LDL cholesterol; heart-outcome results are still awaited
peptides.mechanism: Blocks PCSK9, a liver protein that destroys LDL receptors, so the liver clears more LDL cholesterol from the blood
peptides.summary: Enlicitide (Lipfendra) is the first FDA-approved oral PCSK9 inhibitor, a daily tablet that lowered LDL cholesterol by about 56 points more than placebo in trials. Its effect on heart attacks is still awaited.

peptides.name: Glepaglutide
peptides.route: Injection under the skin, twice weekly in the main trial
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. FDA issued a complete response letter in December 2024; new phase 3 trials began in 2025-2026
peptides.mechanism: Long-acting copy of GLP-2, a gut hormone that helps the small intestine grow and absorb more fluid and nutrients
uses: Short bowel syndrome with intestinal failure
peptides.summary: Glepaglutide is an investigational GLP-2 injection for short bowel syndrome. A phase 3 trial showed less need for IV nutrition on the twice-weekly dose, but the FDA asked for another trial in December 2024.

peptides.name: Larazotide acetate
peptides.route: Taken by mouth, three times a day in trials
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. The only phase 3 trial was stopped by the sponsor in 2022 after an interim analysis
peptides.mechanism: A short peptide meant to keep the tight junctions between gut lining cells closed, limiting leakage of gluten fragments into the gut wall
uses: Celiac disease symptoms despite a gluten-free diet (studied)
peptides.summary: Larazotide acetate is an experimental peptide that aims to tighten the gut lining in celiac disease. Early trials gave mixed symptom results, its phase 3 trial was stopped in 2022, and it is not approved.

peptides.name: Mazdutide
peptides.route: Once-weekly injection under the skin
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. Approved in China for weight management in June 2025; US trials so far are early-phase
peptides.mechanism: Activates both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors to lower appetite and raise the liver's use of fat
peptides.summary: Mazdutide is a once-weekly GLP-1 and glucagon dual agonist approved in China in 2025 for weight management. Chinese phase 3 trials show 14-17% weight loss, but it is not approved in the US.

peptides.name: PN-943
peptides.cls: Oral alpha-4 beta-7 integrin antagonist peptide
peptides.route: Taken by mouth twice a day in trials
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. A phase 2 ulcerative colitis trial reported in 2022; no phase 3 trial is registered
peptides.mechanism: Blocks the alpha-4 beta-7 integrin on gut-homing immune cells so fewer enter the intestinal lining, acting mainly inside the gut
peptides.summary: PN-943 is an experimental oral peptide that blocks the alpha-4 beta-7 integrin to keep immune cells out of the inflamed gut. A phase 2 ulcerative colitis trial showed a modest signal, and it is not approved.

peptides.name: Pemvidutide
peptides.route: Once-weekly injection under the skin in trials
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. Phase 2 trials in MASH are complete; a phase 3 MASH trial began recruiting in July 2026
peptides.mechanism: Balanced GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist that lowers appetite and acts on the liver to reduce fat and inflammation
peptides.summary: Pemvidutide is an investigational once-weekly GLP-1 and glucagon dual agonist aimed at fatty liver disease with inflammation (MASH). Phase 2 trials cut liver fat sharply, and a phase 3 trial began in 2026.

peptides.name: Petrelintide
peptides.route: Once-weekly injection under the skin in trials
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. Phase 2 trials are complete; Roche began phase 3 trials in 2026
peptides.mechanism: Long-acting copy of human amylin, a hormone that signals fullness to the brain through a different pathway than GLP-1 drugs
peptides.summary: Petrelintide is an investigational once-weekly amylin analog for obesity. A 2026 phase 2 trial showed up to about 10% weight loss with mostly mild nausea, and Roche has begun phase 3 trials. It is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Survodutide
peptides.route: Once-weekly injection under the skin in trials
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. Phase 3 obesity results reported in 2026; MASH phase 3 trials are under way
peptides.mechanism: Activates glucagon and GLP-1 receptors to lower appetite and act directly on the liver to reduce fat and inflammation
peptides.summary: Survodutide is an investigational once-weekly glucagon and GLP-1 dual agonist from Boehringer Ingelheim. Phase 3 trials showed 12-13% weight loss and large liver-fat drops, but it is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: BPC-157
peptides.route: Injected or swallowed in unregulated products; no approved form
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. FDA advisers voted 8-6 in July 2026 to allow compounding; the FDA has not yet acted
peptides.mechanism: Animal studies suggest it boosts blood-vessel growth and tissue-repair signals, but how it works in people is not established
peptides.summary: BPC-157 is a lab-made peptide sold online for healing tendons and gut injuries. Evidence is almost entirely from animals, human data are tiny, and it is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: KPV
peptides.route: Oral, injected or topical in unregulated products; no approved form
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. FDA advisers voted 8-6 in July 2026 to allow compounding; the FDA has not yet acted
peptides.mechanism: A three-amino-acid fragment of alpha-MSH that dampens NF-kappaB inflammatory signaling in cells and mouse colitis models
peptides.summary: KPV is a three-amino-acid fragment of the hormone alpha-MSH that calms inflammation in cells and mouse colitis. Human trial data are essentially absent, and it is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: AOD-9604
peptides.route: Injected or swallowed in unregulated products; no approved form
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. Obesity trials did not lead to approval; FDA advisers voted 12-0 against a compounding listing in 2024
peptides.mechanism: A modified piece of the growth hormone molecule that increased fat breakdown in rodents without the blood-sugar effects of whole growth hormone
peptides.summary: AOD-9604 is a modified fragment of human growth hormone sold online for fat loss. It worked in rodents, human obesity trials did not lead to approval, and it is banned in sport and not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: 5-Amino-1MQ
peptides.route: Mostly capsules from unregulated sellers; no approved form
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved and not a peptide. Studied only in cells and mice; no human studies found
peptides.mechanism: Blocks NNMT, an enzyme in fat tissue, which in mice raised NAD+ and cellular energy use and reduced diet-induced obesity
peptides.summary: 5-Amino-1MQ is a small molecule, not a peptide, sold online as a fat-loss and metabolism booster. It blocks an enzyme called NNMT in mice, but no human studies exist and it is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Fragment 176-191
peptides.route: Injected in unregulated products; no approved form
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved. No human trials found; banned in sport and sold online as a research peptide
peptides.mechanism: A piece of the growth hormone tail reported to reduce fat storage and promote fat breakdown in animal and tissue experiments
peptides.summary: Fragment 176-191 is a piece of human growth hormone sold online for fat loss. Evidence is limited to rodent and tissue studies of closely related fragments; it is banned in sport and not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Cyclosporine
peptides.route: Capsules or liquid by mouth, IV infusion in hospital, or eye drops
peptides.status: FDA-approved: transplant rejection prevention, severe rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and dry eye (eye drops)
peptides.mechanism: Binds the protein cyclophilin; the complex blocks calcineurin, stopping T cells from switching on the inflammatory signals that drive rejection
peptides.summary: Cyclosporine is a cyclic peptide immunosuppressant used to prevent organ transplant rejection, treat severe rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and, as eye drops, chronic dry eye.

peptides.name: Enfuvirtide
peptides.route: Injection under the skin, twice a day
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2003) for treatment-experienced HIV-1; Genentech ended U.S. marketing on Feb 28, 2025
peptides.mechanism: Mimics part of the HIV envelope protein gp41 and blocks the folding step the virus needs to fuse with, and enter, immune cells
uses: HIV-1 with ongoing replication despite treatment
peptides.summary: Enfuvirtide (Fuzeon) was the first HIV fusion inhibitor, an injected peptide for multidrug-resistant HIV. Genentech stopped U.S. sales in February 2025 as newer options replaced it.

peptides.name: Polymyxin B / Colistin
peptides.route: Hospital injection (IV or IM); polymyxin B also in eye and skin products
peptides.status: FDA-approved antibiotics for serious Gram-negative infections; polymyxin B injection carries a boxed warning
peptides.mechanism: Positively charged lipopeptides that bind lipopolysaccharide in the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria and disrupt their membranes
uses: Last-resort treatment when other drugs fail
peptides.summary: Polymyxin B and colistin are old injectable antibiotics, now last-line options for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections. They can damage the kidneys and nerves, and resistance is spreading.

peptides.name: Aviptadil
peptides.route: IV infusion in trials; inhaled forms in smaller studies
peptides.status: Investigational; not FDA-approved. COVID-19 trials did not show a clear survival benefit
peptides.mechanism: Synthetic copy of vasoactive intestinal peptide, a natural signal that relaxes blood vessels and calms inflammation, tested to protect the lungs
peptides.summary: Aviptadil is synthetic vasoactive intestinal peptide, studied for lung failure in COVID-19. Two large randomized trials did not show a clear survival benefit, and it is not approved in the US.

peptides.name: Murepavadin
peptides.route: IV in phase 3 trials; an inhaled form has had early testing
peptides.status: Investigational; IV phase 3 trials stopped in 2019 over kidney injury; no FDA approval
peptides.mechanism: A protegrin-inspired ring-shaped peptidomimetic that blocks LptD, the protein that ships lipopolysaccharide to the outer membrane of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
peptides.summary: Murepavadin is an experimental antibiotic aimed at Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Its IV phase 3 trials were halted in 2019 after kidney injury, and an inhaled version has had only early testing.

peptides.name: Nangibotide
peptides.route: Continuous IV infusion in trials
peptides.status: Investigational; phase 2 trials done; FDA-agreed phase 3 design announced Jan 2024; not approved
peptides.mechanism: A 12-amino-acid decoy peptide that traps the ligand of TREM-1, an immune-cell receptor that amplifies inflammation in septic shock
peptides.summary: Nangibotide is an experimental peptide that dampens TREM-1, an inflammation amplifier, in septic shock. Its phase 2b trial missed the main goal; a biomarker-guided phase 3 has been planned.

peptides.name: Thymosin alpha-1
peptides.route: Injection under the skin (in studies and where approved abroad)
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; approved in some other countries; FDA advisers voted against compounding use in Dec 2024
peptides.mechanism: A 28-amino-acid thymic peptide thought to nudge T cells and dendritic cells toward a stronger, better-regulated immune response
peptides.summary: Thymosin alpha-1 is a thymus-derived peptide approved as a drug in some countries, not the US. Trials in sepsis and infections are mixed, and FDA advisers rejected compounding use in 2024.

peptides.name: LL-37
peptides.route: Applied to ulcers in trials; unapproved injections sold online
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA flagged immunogenicity, tumor-promotion and reproductive concerns
peptides.mechanism: The body's own antimicrobial peptide: disrupts microbial membranes and signals immune and repair cells; in excess it can drive skin inflammation
peptides.summary: LL-37 is the human body's own cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide. Topical leg-ulcer trials gave mixed results, while injected use is unapproved and the FDA cites immunogenicity and tumor concerns.

peptides.name: Thymulin
peptides.route: Research use only; no approved product
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA lists thymulin acetate in category 3 (nominated without adequate support)
peptides.mechanism: A nine-amino-acid hormone made by thymus cells that needs zinc to be active; helps T cells mature and calms inflammation, mostly shown in animals
peptides.summary: Thymulin is a nine-amino-acid thymus hormone that needs zinc to work. Research is mostly in animals, there is no approved use, and the FDA lists it as nominated for compounding without adequate support.

peptides.name: Albiglutide
peptides.route: Weekly injection under the skin (no longer sold)
peptides.status: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes (2014); discontinued by its maker in 2017-2018 for commercial, not safety, reasons
peptides.mechanism: Two linked copies of a modified GLP-1 hormone fused to human albumin, which keeps GLP-1 receptors switched on for about a week per dose
peptides.summary: Albiglutide (Tanzeum) was a once-weekly GLP-1 drug approved in 2014 for type 2 diabetes. It cut heart attack and stroke risk in a large trial but left the market in 2018.

peptides.name: Corticotropin
peptides.route: Injection into a muscle or under the skin, daily or every 1-3 days
peptides.status: FDA-approved (Acthar Gel since 1952; Purified Cortrophin Gel relaunched in 2021) for infantile spasms, MS flares and other conditions
peptides.mechanism: Purified pituitary hormone that signals the adrenal glands to make cortisol, damping inflammation; it may also act on immune cells via melanocortin receptors
peptides.summary: Corticotropin (Acthar Gel, Purified Cortrophin Gel) is an injectable form of the pituitary hormone ACTH, FDA-approved for infantile spasms, MS flares and inflammatory diseases.

peptides.name: Cosyntropin
peptides.route: Single injection into a vein or muscle during an adrenal function test
peptides.status: FDA-approved for diagnostic use only: screening for adrenal insufficiency (Cortrosyn and generic versions)
peptides.mechanism: Copies the first 24 amino acids of ACTH, which prompt healthy adrenal glands to release cortisol within an hour, revealing whether they can respond
peptides.summary: Cosyntropin (Cortrosyn) is a synthetic piece of the hormone ACTH used in the ACTH stimulation test, the standard FDA-approved way to check whether the adrenal glands make enough cortisol.

peptides.name: Dulaglutide
peptides.route: Once-weekly injection under the skin from a single-dose pen
peptides.status: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes in adults (2014) and children 10 and older (2022), and to lower cardiovascular risk
peptides.mechanism: Two GLP-1-like peptides joined to an antibody fragment, which raise insulin when glucose is high, curb glucagon and slow stomach emptying for a week
uses: Type 2 diabetes in children 10 and older
Lowering heart attack and stroke risk
peptides.summary: Dulaglutide (Trulicity) is a once-weekly GLP-1 injection for type 2 diabetes in adults and children 10 and older, also approved to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke.

peptides.name: Exenatide
peptides.route: Injection under the skin twice daily before meals (a weekly form is no longer sold)
peptides.status: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes since 2005; Byetta and Bydureon BCise brands discontinued in 2024, generic twice-daily form remains
peptides.mechanism: Synthetic copy of a Gila monster venom peptide that activates GLP-1 receptors, raising insulin when glucose is high and slowing stomach emptying
peptides.summary: Exenatide was the first GLP-1 drug, approved in 2005 for type 2 diabetes. Its Byetta and Bydureon brands were discontinued in 2024, but a generic twice-daily version remains.

peptides.name: Insulin analogs (multiple)
peptides.route: Injection under the skin by pen, syringe or pump; regular insulin can also be given IV
peptides.status: FDA-approved for type 1 and type 2 diabetes; first weekly basal insulins (icodec, efsitora) approved in 2026 for adults with type 2 diabetes
peptides.mechanism: Lab-made insulins with small structural changes that make them act faster or last longer, replacing the insulin the pancreas no longer makes in sufficient amounts
uses: Hospital treatment of high blood sugar
peptides.summary: Insulin analogs are modified insulins, from rapid-acting mealtime types to daily and new once-weekly basal insulins, used to treat type 1 and type 2 diabetes in the US.

peptides.name: Lixisenatide
peptides.route: Once-daily injection under the skin within an hour before the first meal
peptides.status: FDA-approved 2016; standalone Adlyxin discontinued in 2023, still sold combined with insulin glargine as Soliqua 100/33
peptides.mechanism: Short-acting exendin-4-based GLP-1 agonist that mainly blunts the blood sugar rise after meals by slowing stomach emptying and boosting insulin
uses: Type 2 diabetes (with insulin glargine in Soliqua)
peptides.summary: Lixisenatide is a short-acting, once-daily GLP-1 drug for type 2 diabetes. Sold alone as Adlyxin until 2023, it is now available in the US only in Soliqua 100/33.

peptides.name: Mecasermin
peptides.route: Injection under the skin twice daily, within 20 minutes of a meal or snack
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2005) for growth failure in children 2 and older with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency
peptides.mechanism: Lab-made copy of IGF-1, the growth factor that growth hormone normally triggers, given directly when the body cannot respond to growth hormone
uses: Severe primary IGF-1 deficiency (such as Laron syndrome)
GH gene deletion with growth hormone antibodies
peptides.summary: Mecasermin (Increlex) is lab-made IGF-1, FDA-approved for children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency whose bodies cannot respond to growth hormone. It is given by injection twice daily.

peptides.name: Pasireotide
peptides.route: Twice-daily injection under the skin, or a monthly muscle injection given in a clinic
peptides.status: FDA-approved (since 2012) for Cushing's disease and acromegaly when pituitary surgery is not an option or has not worked
peptides.mechanism: Mimics the hormone somatostatin at several receptor types, especially SSTR5, to turn down ACTH and growth hormone release from pituitary tumors
peptides.summary: Pasireotide (Signifor, Signifor LAR) is a somatostatin analog for Cushing's disease and acromegaly when pituitary surgery is not an option or has failed. High blood sugar is its main drawback.

peptides.name: Pegvisomant
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin after a supervised loading dose
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2003) for acromegaly not controlled by surgery or radiation
peptides.mechanism: Modified growth hormone that occupies the growth hormone receptor without switching it on, so the liver makes far less IGF-1
peptides.summary: Pegvisomant (Somavert) is a daily injection for acromegaly that blocks the growth hormone receptor, normalizing IGF-1 in most patients when surgery or radiation has not worked.

peptides.name: Pramlintide
peptides.route: Injection under the skin immediately before major meals
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2005) as an add-on to mealtime insulin in adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes; boxed warning for severe hypoglycemia
peptides.mechanism: Stable copy of amylin, a hormone released with insulin, that slows stomach emptying, curbs glucagon after meals and increases fullness
peptides.summary: Pramlintide (SymlinPen) is an injectable copy of the hormone amylin, approved since 2005 as an add-on to mealtime insulin to smooth post-meal blood sugar in type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

peptides.name: Secretin
peptides.route: Single injection into a vein over one minute during a diagnostic test
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2004) as a diagnostic aid for pancreatic function, gastrinoma and locating duct openings during ERCP
peptides.mechanism: Copy of the gut hormone secretin, which makes the pancreas pour out bicarbonate-rich fluid and makes gastrinomas release a burst of gastrin
peptides.summary: Secretin (ChiRhoStim) is a synthetic copy of a gut hormone used in diagnostic tests of pancreatic function and gastrinoma. It is FDA-approved for testing only and did not help autism in trials.

peptides.name: Somapacitan
peptides.route: Once-weekly injection under the skin from a prefilled pen
peptides.status: FDA-approved: adult GH deficiency (2020), childhood GH deficiency (2023), plus SGA, Noonan syndrome and idiopathic short stature (2026)
peptides.mechanism: Growth hormone carrying a small albumin-binding side chain that slows its clearance, so one weekly injection can replace daily shots
uses: Short stature after being born small for gestational age
peptides.summary: Somapacitan (Sogroya) is a once-weekly growth hormone for adults and children with growth hormone deficiency, and since 2026 for several other causes of short stature in children.

peptides.name: Somatropin (rhGH)
peptides.route: Injection under the skin, usually once a day, from a pen or vial
peptides.status: FDA-approved for childhood growth disorders and adult GH deficiency; use for anti-aging or sport is not approved
peptides.mechanism: Replaces the pituitary hormone that drives childhood growth and, through IGF-1, shapes muscle, fat and sugar metabolism in adults
uses: Growth failure from GH deficiency in children
peptides.summary: Somatropin is lab-made human growth hormone, approved for children with growth failure and adults with true GH deficiency, and prohibited in sport. It is not an approved anti-aging drug.

peptides.name: Efpeglenatide
peptides.route: Weekly injection under the skin (in trials)
peptides.status: Investigational, not FDA-approved: phase 3 trials in obesity (completed) and type 2 diabetes (recruiting)
peptides.mechanism: Exendin-4 based GLP-1 drug attached to an antibody fragment so it lasts a week, raising insulin when glucose is high and easing appetite
uses: Lowering heart and kidney event risk (studied)
peptides.summary: Efpeglenatide is a once-weekly GLP-1 drug still in development for obesity and type 2 diabetes. A large trial showed fewer cardiovascular events, but it is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Elamipretide
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin
peptides.status: FDA accelerated approval (Sept 2025) for Barth syndrome; other uses still in trials
peptides.mechanism: Binds cardiolipin, a lipid in the inner membrane of mitochondria, to steady the cell's energy-producing machinery
peptides.summary: Elamipretide (Forzinity) is a mitochondria-targeting peptide with FDA accelerated approval for Barth syndrome since 2025. Trials in other mitochondrial and eye diseases are mixed or ongoing.

peptides.name: MOTS-c
aliases: Mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA-c
peptides.route: Injection under the skin in research and gray-market use
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA advisers backed pharmacy compounding in July 2026, decision pending; banned in sport by WADA
peptides.mechanism: A 16-amino-acid peptide encoded in mitochondrial DNA that, in mice, switches on the energy sensor AMPK and improves insulin sensitivity
peptides.summary: MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid peptide made by mitochondria. Mouse studies suggest metabolic benefits, but controlled human trials are lacking, and it is unapproved and banned in sport.

peptides.name: Tesamorelin (off-label)
peptides.route: Injection under the skin; compounded copies are unapproved
peptides.status: Approved as Egrifta only for abdominal fat in HIV lipodystrophy; compounded and wellness use is off-label and unapproved
peptides.mechanism: Stimulates the pituitary to release growth hormone, which raises IGF-1 and shrinks deep belly fat in people with HIV lipodystrophy
uses: Visceral fat loss (approved only in HIV lipodystrophy)
peptides.summary: Tesamorelin is FDA-approved as Egrifta only to cut belly fat in adults with HIV lipodystrophy. Clinics also sell off-label or compounded versions for anti-aging and fat loss, without approval or proof.

peptides.name: Humanin
peptides.route: Injection in research and gray-market use
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved and not on FDA compounding lists; no human trials; WADA bans non-approved drugs like it
peptides.mechanism: A short peptide encoded in mitochondrial DNA that protects cells from stress-induced death and, in animals, improves insulin sensitivity
peptides.summary: Humanin is a short mitochondrial peptide first found in a screen for Alzheimer's protection. Evidence comes from cells and animals, no human trials exist, and it is not FDA-approved.

peptides.name: Abaloparatide
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin from a prefilled pen
peptides.status: FDA-approved for osteoporosis at high fracture risk in postmenopausal women and in men
peptides.mechanism: Activates the parathyroid hormone receptor on bone-forming cells to build new bone instead of only slowing bone loss
uses: Postmenopausal osteoporosis at high fracture risk
Osteoporosis in men at high fracture risk
When other osteoporosis drugs failed or were not tolerated
peptides.summary: Abaloparatide (Tymlos) is a daily bone-building injection for people with osteoporosis at high fracture risk. It sharply cut new spine fractures in postmenopausal women in a major trial.

peptides.name: Calcitonin-salmon
peptides.route: Injection under the skin or into a muscle; nasal sprays were also approved
peptides.status: FDA-approved (injection since 1975) for Paget's disease, hypercalcemia and, if other options are unsuitable, osteoporosis
peptides.mechanism: Mimics the thyroid hormone calcitonin to slow the osteoclasts that dissolve bone and to lower blood calcium
uses: Postmenopausal osteoporosis when alternatives are unsuitable
peptides.summary: Salmon calcitonin (Miacalcin) is a hormone injection that slows bone breakdown and lowers blood calcium. It is used for Paget's disease, high calcium and, when other options are unsuitable, osteoporosis.

peptides.name: Etelcalcetide
peptides.route: Intravenous injection at the end of each dialysis session
peptides.status: FDA-approved for secondary hyperparathyroidism in adults with chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis
peptides.mechanism: Activates the calcium-sensing receptor on parathyroid cells, which lowers parathyroid hormone release and blood calcium
uses: Secondary hyperparathyroidism in adults on hemodialysis
peptides.summary: Etelcalcetide (Parsabiv) is an injected peptide that lowers high parathyroid hormone in adults on hemodialysis. It outperformed placebo and the oral drug cinacalcet in trials; low blood calcium is the main risk.

peptides.name: Palopegteriparatide
peptides.route: Once-daily injection under the skin from a prefilled pen
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2024) for hypoparathyroidism in adults
peptides.mechanism: A slowly releasing form of PTH(1-34) that replaces the missing parathyroid hormone steadily across the day
peptides.summary: Palopegteriparatide (Yorvipath) is a once-daily, long-acting parathyroid hormone for adults with hypoparathyroidism. In a phase 3 trial most people no longer needed standard calcium and active vitamin D therapy.

peptides.name: Parathyroid hormone
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin (no longer supplied)
peptides.status: FDA-approved in 2015 for hypoparathyroidism, but discontinued: manufacturing ended Dec 2024, US access program closed Dec 2025
peptides.mechanism: Replaces the full-length parathyroid hormone that people with hypoparathyroidism lack, helping hold blood calcium in range
peptides.summary: Natpara was recombinant parathyroid hormone (1-84), approved in 2015 for hypoparathyroidism. It worked in a phase 3 trial, but its maker stopped manufacturing it and the last US access program closed in 2025.

peptides.name: Teriparatide
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin from a prefilled pen
peptides.status: FDA-approved for osteoporosis at high fracture risk in postmenopausal women, in men, and from long-term steroid use
peptides.mechanism: Copies the first 34 amino acids of parathyroid hormone; daily pulses switch on bone-forming cells and build new bone
uses: Postmenopausal osteoporosis at high fracture risk
Bone mass in men with primary or hypogonadal osteoporosis
peptides.summary: Teriparatide (Forteo) is a daily injection that builds new bone in people with osteoporosis at high fracture risk. It cut spine fractures sharply in trials, and its osteosarcoma boxed warning was removed in 2020.

peptides.name: Vosoritide
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin, with the dose set by body weight
peptides.status: FDA accelerated approval to increase linear growth in children with achondroplasia who have open growth plates
peptides.mechanism: Mimics C-type natriuretic peptide, which dampens the overactive FGFR3 growth-plate signal in achondroplasia and so promotes bone growth
uses: Achondroplasia in children with open growth plates
peptides.summary: Vosoritide (Voxzogo) is a daily injection that speeds growth in children with achondroplasia whose growth plates are open. It is approved on an accelerated basis, and final adult height effects are still being established.

peptides.name: Zilucoplan
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin from a prefilled syringe
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2023) for generalized myasthenia gravis in adults with anti-AChR antibodies; boxed warning for meningococcal infection
peptides.mechanism: Binds complement protein C5 and blocks its cleavage, cutting off the immune attack on the nerve-muscle junction that drives weakness
peptides.summary: Zilucoplan (Zilbrysq) is a daily self-injected peptide that blocks complement C5 in adults with anti-AChR-positive generalized myasthenia gravis. It carries a boxed warning for serious meningococcal infections.

peptides.name: TB-500
peptides.route: Injection under the skin in research and gray-market use
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA advisers backed pharmacy compounding in July 2026, decision pending; banned in sport by WADA
peptides.mechanism: A short synthetic piece of thymosin beta-4 that binds actin and is claimed to speed tissue repair, though human evidence is lacking
peptides.summary: TB-500 is a synthetic fragment of thymosin beta-4 sold for injury recovery. No controlled human trials of it were found; it is not FDA-approved and WADA bans it at all times.

peptides.name: CJC-1295
peptides.route: Injection under the skin in research and gray-market use
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA advisers voted against pharmacy compounding in 2024; its safety-risk listing was removed in 2026; banned in sport
peptides.mechanism: A modified growth hormone-releasing hormone that, in its DAC form, binds albumin to act for days and keep growth hormone and IGF-1 raised
peptides.summary: CJC-1295 is a long-acting GHRH analog that raised GH and IGF-1 in small human studies. No trials show muscle, fat-loss or anti-aging benefits; it is unapproved and banned in sport.

peptides.name: Ipamorelin
peptides.route: Injection under the skin in research and gray-market use
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA cited safety concerns in 2023 and removed its 503A Category 2 listing in April 2026; banned in sport
peptides.mechanism: A five-amino-acid peptide that activates the ghrelin receptor to trigger growth hormone release, with little effect on cortisol in early animal studies
peptides.summary: Ipamorelin is a five-amino-acid peptide that triggers growth hormone release. Human data are limited and show no clear benefit for the claimed uses; it is unapproved and banned in sport.

peptides.name: Sermorelin
peptides.route: Injection under the skin (compounded products)
peptides.status: Not currently FDA-approved: Geref was approved in 1990 and 1997, discontinued in 2008; compounded versions are unapproved
peptides.mechanism: The first 29 amino acids of growth hormone-releasing hormone, which tell the pituitary to release growth hormone in pulses
peptides.summary: Sermorelin is the first 29 amino acids of GHRH. The FDA approved it as Geref until the maker discontinued it in 2008; today compounding pharmacies sell it for anti-aging with limited adult evidence.

peptides.name: MK-677 (ibutamoren)
peptides.route: Taken by mouth; no approved product
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA lists ibutamoren in Category 2 (significant safety risks) for compounding; banned in sport
peptides.mechanism: A non-peptide drug that mimics the hunger hormone ghrelin to raise growth hormone and IGF-1 when swallowed
peptides.summary: MK-677 (ibutamoren) is an oral drug, not a peptide, that raises growth hormone and IGF-1. Trials showed more lean mass but weight gain, higher blood sugar and a heart failure signal; it is unapproved and banned in sport.

peptides.name: Thymosin beta-4
peptides.route: Injection, gel or eye drops in trials; injection in gray-market use
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; studied in eye, skin and heart conditions; banned in sport by WADA
peptides.mechanism: A natural 43-amino-acid peptide that binds actin and is thought to speed cell migration, new blood vessel growth and repair after injury
peptides.summary: Thymosin beta-4 is a natural 43-amino-acid repair peptide studied for wounds, eyes and the heart. No product is FDA-approved, human data are limited, and WADA bans it.

peptides.name: Follistatin-344
peptides.route: Injection in gray-market use; virus-delivered gene therapy in trials
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved in any form; only experimental gene therapy has been tested in people; banned in sport by WADA
peptides.mechanism: Binds myostatin and related activin signals that restrain muscle growth, so blocking them increases muscle mass in animals
peptides.summary: Follistatin-344 is a large protein that blocks myostatin, a brake on muscle growth. Engineered mice grow huge muscles, but human data are limited to gene therapy trials; it is unapproved and banned in sport.

peptides.name: GHRP-2
peptides.route: Injection under the skin in research and gray-market use
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved (used as a diagnostic test in Japan); FDA Category 3: nominated without adequate support; banned in sport
peptides.mechanism: A six-amino-acid peptide that activates the ghrelin receptor to trigger a strong growth hormone surge and raise appetite
peptides.summary: GHRP-2 (pralmorelin) is a six-amino-acid peptide that triggers growth hormone release and hunger. It has no FDA approval, the FDA cites serious safety reports, and WADA bans it.

peptides.name: GHRP-6
peptides.route: Injection under the skin in research and gray-market use
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA Category 3 (nominated without adequate support) and safety concerns cited; banned in sport
peptides.mechanism: A six-amino-acid peptide, the first of its family studied widely in people, that activates the ghrelin receptor to release growth hormone
peptides.summary: GHRP-6 is a six-amino-acid peptide that triggers growth hormone release and hunger. Human data are short hormone studies; it is unapproved, the FDA cites safety concerns, and WADA bans it.

peptides.name: Hexarelin
peptides.route: Injection under the skin in research and gray-market use
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved and not on FDA's compounding nomination lists; banned in sport by WADA
peptides.mechanism: A potent six-amino-acid peptide that releases growth hormone through the ghrelin receptor, but its effect fades with repeated use
peptides.summary: Hexarelin is a potent six-amino-acid peptide that triggers growth hormone release, but its effect faded within weeks in a human trial. It is unapproved and banned in sport.

peptides.name: IGF-1 DES
peptides.route: Injection in research and gray-market use
peptides.status: Never approved for human use; sold as a research chemical and black-market product; banned in sport by WADA
peptides.mechanism: IGF-1 missing its first three amino acids, so it binds IGF-binding proteins poorly and acts about ten times more strongly in cell studies
peptides.summary: IGF-1 DES is a truncated, more potent form of insulin-like growth factor 1 sold for muscle growth. It was never approved for people, can lower blood sugar strongly, and is banned in sport.

peptides.name: IGF-1 LR3
peptides.route: Injection in research and gray-market use
peptides.status: Never approved for human use; sold as a research chemical and black-market product; banned in sport by WADA
peptides.mechanism: An engineered IGF-1 with an arginine swap at position 3 and an extended front end, so it binds IGF-binding proteins poorly and stays active longer
peptides.summary: IGF-1 LR3 is an engineered, longer-acting form of insulin-like growth factor 1 sold for muscle growth. It was never approved for people, can lower blood sugar in animals, and is banned in sport.

peptides.name: Mechano growth factor
peptides.route: Injection in research and gray-market use
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA Category 3 (nominated without adequate support); banned in sport by WADA
peptides.mechanism: The tail (E domain) of a muscle IGF-1 splice variant that rises after exercise; proposed to activate muscle stem cells, but one replication attempt found no effect
peptides.summary: Mechano growth factor (MGF) is a muscle IGF-1 splice variant whose tail peptide is sold as PEG-MGF. One lab reported effects in cells; others could not reproduce them, and no human trials exist.

peptides.name: Angiotensin II
peptides.route: Continuous intravenous infusion in an intensive care setting
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2017) to raise blood pressure in adults with septic or other distributive shock
peptides.mechanism: Copies the body's own pressure-raising hormone, which tightens blood vessels through AT1 receptors and signals the adrenal glands to retain salt and water
peptides.summary: Angiotensin II (Giapreza) is a hospital-only intravenous hormone that raises blood pressure in adults with septic or other distributive shock. The FDA approved it in 2017.

peptides.name: Bivalirudin
peptides.route: Intravenous bolus followed by an infusion during the procedure
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2000) as an anticoagulant during angioplasty and stenting; generics are widely available
peptides.mechanism: Binds thrombin directly at two sites and blocks it, so blood clots cannot form, without needing antithrombin; the effect wears off within about an hour
uses: PCI in people with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
peptides.summary: Bivalirudin (Angiomax) is a short-acting intravenous blood thinner given during angioplasty and stent procedures, including in people who cannot receive heparin.

peptides.name: Desirudin
peptides.route: Injection under the skin every 12 hours around hip replacement surgery
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2003) to prevent deep vein clots after hip replacement; the US brand has been discontinued
peptides.mechanism: A lab-made copy of leech hirudin that binds thrombin tightly and blocks it, which stops clots from forming without needing antithrombin
uses: Preventing DVT after elective hip replacement
peptides.summary: Desirudin (Iprivask) is a lab-made form of leech hirudin that the FDA approved in 2003 as an injected blood thinner after hip replacement. The US brand has since been discontinued.

peptides.name: Desmopressin
peptides.route: Injection, nasal spray or tablet, depending on the condition
peptides.status: FDA-approved (first in 1978) for diabetes insipidus, bedwetting, mild hemophilia A and type 1 von Willebrand disease
peptides.mechanism: Mimics vasopressin's action in the kidney to concentrate urine and triggers release of factor VIII and von Willebrand factor, with little effect on blood pressure
uses: Mild hemophilia A and type 1 von Willebrand disease
peptides.summary: Desmopressin (DDAVP, Stimate) is a lab-made vasopressin analog that concentrates urine and raises clotting factors, used for diabetes insipidus, bedwetting, mild bleeding disorders and nocturia.

peptides.name: Echinocandins
peptides.route: IV infusion: daily (caspofungin, micafungin, anidulafungin) or weekly (rezafungin)
peptides.status: FDA-approved: caspofungin (2001), micafungin (2005), anidulafungin (2006), rezafungin (2023)
peptides.mechanism: Block glucan synthase, the enzyme fungi use to build their cell wall, so the wall weakens and the fungal cell bursts; human cells have no such enzyme
uses: Invasive aspergillosis when other drugs fail
Preventing Candida infection in stem cell transplant
peptides.summary: Echinocandins (caspofungin, micafungin, anidulafungin, rezafungin) are intravenous antifungal drugs and the usual first treatment for serious Candida bloodstream infections.

peptides.name: Eptifibatide
peptides.route: Intravenous bolus followed by a continuous infusion in a hospital
peptides.status: FDA-approved (1998) for acute coronary syndromes and angioplasty or stenting; generic versions are sold
peptides.mechanism: Blocks the platelet receptor glycoprotein IIb/IIIa so platelets cannot bind fibrinogen and join together, which keeps clots in heart arteries from growing
uses: Unstable angina and non-ST-elevation heart attack
peptides.summary: Eptifibatide (Integrilin) is an intravenous platelet blocker used in hospital for acute coronary syndromes and during angioplasty or stenting to lower the risk of heart attack.

peptides.name: Motixafortide
