peptides.route: Slow injection under the skin the night before stem cell collection, with filgrastim
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2023) with filgrastim to mobilize stem cells for collection in multiple myeloma
peptides.mechanism: Blocks the CXCR4 receptor that anchors blood stem cells in the bone marrow, so more stem cells move into the bloodstream where they can be collected
uses: Stem cell collection before transplant in myeloma
peptides.summary: Motixafortide (Aphexda) is a CXCR4-blocking peptide given with filgrastim to push blood stem cells out of the bone marrow so they can be collected for a transplant in multiple myeloma.

peptides.name: Nesiritide
peptides.route: Intravenous bolus followed by a continuous infusion in a hospital
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2001) for acute decompensated heart failure; the Natrecor brand is discontinued
peptides.mechanism: A lab-made copy of the heart hormone BNP that relaxes blood vessels, lowering the pressure the heart works against, and promotes salt and water loss
uses: Acute decompensated heart failure with breathlessness
peptides.summary: Nesiritide (Natrecor) is a lab-made version of the heart hormone BNP, approved in 2001 for acute heart failure. Large trials showed little benefit, and it is no longer sold in the US.

peptides.name: Pegcetacoplan
peptides.route: Infusion under the skin twice weekly (Empaveli); injection into the eye (Syfovre)
peptides.status: FDA-approved: Empaveli for PNH (2021) and C3 glomerulopathy or IC-MPGN (2025); Syfovre for geographic atrophy (2023)
peptides.mechanism: Binds complement proteins C3 and C3b to switch off the complement cascade at its center, which curbs red blood cell destruction, kidney inflammation and retinal cell loss
uses: Geographic atrophy from age-related macular degeneration
peptides.summary: Pegcetacoplan (Empaveli, Syfovre) is a PEGylated peptide that blocks complement protein C3, approved for PNH and two kidney diseases by infusion and for geographic atrophy as an eye injection.

peptides.name: Vancomycin
peptides.route: IV infusion for bloodstream and deep infections; by mouth for C. difficile colitis
peptides.status: FDA-approved: IV for serious Gram-positive infections, oral for C. difficile colitis; many generics
peptides.mechanism: Binds the D-Ala-D-Ala ends of cell wall building blocks and blocks wall construction, killing Gram-positive bacteria including MRSA
uses: Serious MRSA and other Gram-positive infections
peptides.summary: Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic given by IV for serious Gram-positive infections such as MRSA, and by mouth for C. difficile colitis. It has been in clinical use for over 50 years.

peptides.name: Vasopressin
peptides.cls: Hormone; V1 and V2 vasopressin receptor agonist
peptides.route: Continuous intravenous infusion in a hospital
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2014) to raise blood pressure in vasodilatory shock that persists despite fluids and catecholamines
peptides.mechanism: Replaces the pituitary hormone that narrows blood vessels through V1 receptors and makes the kidneys hold water through V2 receptors
peptides.summary: Vasopressin (Vasostrict) is an intravenous hormone given in intensive care to raise blood pressure in vasodilatory shock, usually added to norepinephrine in septic shock.

peptides.name: Balixafortide
peptides.route: Intravenous infusion given with chemotherapy
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; the phase 3 FORTRESS trial in breast cancer was stopped in 2021 after missing its main goal
peptides.mechanism: Designed to block the CXCR4 receptor that helps cancer and immune cells move and settle in tissues, with the aim of making chemotherapy work better
uses: Studied in HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer
peptides.summary: Balixafortide is an experimental CXCR4-blocking peptide tested with the chemotherapy eribulin in metastatic breast cancer. The phase 3 FORTRESS trial showed no benefit, and it is not approved.

peptides.name: Rusfertide
peptides.route: Injection under the skin once weekly
peptides.status: FDA-approved August 28, 2026 (Mimrylo) for erythrocytosis in adults with polycythemia vera
peptides.mechanism: Mimics hepcidin, the liver hormone that controls iron, to limit the iron available for making red blood cells and so curb their overproduction
peptides.summary: Rusfertide (Mimrylo) is a weekly under-the-skin peptide that mimics hepcidin. The FDA approved it in August 2026 to control the excess red blood cells of polycythemia vera.

peptides.name: Selepressin
peptides.route: Continuous intravenous infusion in a hospital
peptides.status: Investigational and discontinued; the phase 2b/3 SEPSIS-ACT trial in septic shock was stopped for futility
peptides.mechanism: Activates vasopressin V1a receptors to tighten blood vessels while avoiding V2 receptors, aiming to raise pressure and limit fluid leakage in sepsis
peptides.summary: Selepressin is an experimental vasopressin-like drug that targets only V1a receptors. It was tested in septic shock, but the large SEPSIS-ACT trial was stopped for futility and it is not approved.

peptides.name: Cetrorelix
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin during ovarian stimulation for IVF
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2000) to prevent premature LH surges in women undergoing controlled ovarian stimulation
peptides.mechanism: Blocks the pituitary's GnRH receptor at once, so LH cannot surge early and release eggs before they are retrieved
uses: Preventing premature LH surges during IVF stimulation
peptides.summary: Cetrorelix (Cetrotide) is a GnRH antagonist injection used in IVF to stop the body from releasing eggs too early during ovarian stimulation. The FDA approved it in 2000.

peptides.name: Degarelix
peptides.route: Monthly injection under the skin of the abdomen
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2008) for advanced prostate cancer
peptides.mechanism: Blocks the pituitary's GnRH receptor directly, so LH and testosterone fall within days with no initial hormone surge
peptides.summary: Degarelix (Firmagon) is a GnRH antagonist injected monthly under the skin to lower testosterone quickly, without the initial surge, in men with advanced prostate cancer.

peptides.name: Ganirelix
peptides.route: Daily injection under the skin during ovarian stimulation for IVF
peptides.status: FDA-approved (1999) to prevent premature LH surges in women undergoing controlled ovarian hyperstimulation; many generics
peptides.mechanism: Competitively blocks the pituitary's GnRH receptor, suppressing LH immediately so an early LH surge cannot release eggs before retrieval
uses: Preventing premature LH surges during IVF stimulation
peptides.summary: Ganirelix is a GnRH antagonist injection used in IVF to stop the body from releasing eggs too early during ovarian stimulation. The FDA approved it in 1999, and generic versions are widely available.

peptides.name: Goserelin
peptides.route: Small implant placed under the skin of the abdomen every 4 or 12 weeks
peptides.status: FDA-approved since 1989 for prostate and breast cancer, endometriosis and endometrial thinning
peptides.mechanism: A slow-release GnRH analog that first stimulates and then desensitizes the pituitary, lowering testosterone in men and estrogen in women
uses: Prostate cancer, with radiotherapy or palliative
peptides.summary: Goserelin (Zoladex) is a GnRH agonist implant that lowers testosterone or estrogen, used for prostate cancer, advanced premenopausal breast cancer, endometriosis and endometrial thinning.

peptides.name: Histrelin
peptides.route: Small implant placed under the skin of the upper arm and replaced yearly
peptides.status: FDA-approved: Supprelin LA (2007) for central precocious puberty; the prostate cancer implant Vantas (2004) is discontinued
peptides.mechanism: Releases a GnRH analog continuously for a year, which first stimulates and then silences the pituitary, shutting down puberty hormones or testosterone
peptides.summary: Histrelin (Supprelin LA) is a GnRH agonist implant placed in the upper arm that suppresses puberty hormones for a year in children with central precocious puberty. Its prostate cancer version, Vantas, is discontinued.

peptides.name: Human chorionic gonadotropin
peptides.route: Injection into a muscle
peptides.status: FDA-approved for undescended testes, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in males and ovulation induction; never approved for weight loss
peptides.mechanism: Acts like luteinizing hormone (LH): it prompts the testes to make testosterone and sperm and triggers ovulation in women
peptides.summary: Human chorionic gonadotropin (Pregnyl, Novarel) is a pregnancy hormone given by injection for undescended testes, some forms of male hypogonadism and ovulation induction. It is not approved for weight loss.

peptides.name: Leuprolide
peptides.route: Depot injection by a clinician every 1 to 6 months, into muscle or under the skin
peptides.status: FDA-approved since 1985 for advanced prostate cancer, endometriosis, uterine fibroids and central precocious puberty
peptides.mechanism: Keeps the pituitary's GnRH receptors switched on, causing a brief surge and then a shutdown of LH and FSH release, which lowers testosterone and estrogen
peptides.summary: Leuprolide (Lupron Depot, Eligard, Fensolvi, Camcevi) is a long-acting GnRH agonist injection that lowers testosterone or estrogen, used for prostate cancer, endometriosis, fibroids and early puberty.

peptides.name: Lutetium Lu-177 vipivotide tetraxetan
peptides.route: Intravenous injection every 6 weeks, up to 6 doses
peptides.status: FDA-approved (2022) for PSMA-positive metastatic prostate cancer; label widened in July 2026 to hormone-sensitive disease
peptides.mechanism: Radioactive lutetium-177 attached to a PSMA-binding molecule, delivering radiation directly to prostate cancer cells and their neighbors
uses: PSMA-positive hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, with ARPI
peptides.summary: Pluvicto (lutetium Lu-177 vipivotide tetraxetan) delivers radiation to PSMA-positive prostate cancer cells. It extended survival in advanced disease and is now approved for earlier-stage disease too.

peptides.name: Nafarelin
peptides.route: Nasal spray, used daily
peptides.status: FDA-approved for endometriosis (6-month course, adult women) and for central precocious puberty in children
peptides.mechanism: A long-lasting copy of GnRH that first stimulates, then shuts down, the pituitary's LH and FSH release, lowering estrogen and testosterone
peptides.summary: Nafarelin (Synarel) is a nasal-spray GnRH agonist that lowers sex hormones. It is approved to manage endometriosis for six months and to treat central precocious puberty in children.

peptides.name: Oxytocin
peptides.route: IV infusion in a hospital; IM injection after delivery
peptides.status: FDA-approved (Pitocin and generics) for medically indicated labor induction and postpartum bleeding; not for elective induction
peptides.mechanism: Synthetic copy of the pituitary hormone oxytocin that binds uterine receptors, raising calcium in muscle cells so the uterus contracts
uses: Adjunct in incomplete or inevitable miscarriage
peptides.summary: Oxytocin (Pitocin) is a hospital hormone drug that starts or strengthens labor for medical reasons and controls bleeding after birth. It is not approved for elective induction.

peptides.name: Triptorelin
peptides.route: Depot injection into a buttock muscle every 4, 12 or 24 weeks
peptides.status: FDA-approved for advanced prostate cancer (Trelstar) and central precocious puberty from age 2 (Triptodur)
peptides.mechanism: A long-acting GnRH analog that desensitizes the pituitary after a brief surge, suppressing LH, FSH and the sex hormones they control
peptides.summary: Triptorelin (Trelstar, Triptodur) is a long-acting GnRH agonist injection that lowers testosterone or estrogen, approved for advanced prostate cancer and for central precocious puberty in children.

peptides.name: Kisspeptin-10
peptides.route: Research injections or infusions; no approved product
peptides.status: Not FDA-approved; FDA category 2 (significant safety risks) for compounding; prohibited by WADA in males
peptides.mechanism: The shortest fully active piece of kisspeptin; it activates the kisspeptin receptor on GnRH neurons, which raises LH, FSH and, in men, testosterone
peptides.summary: Kisspeptin-10 is a fragment of a brain hormone that switches on the reproductive axis. Small human studies show it raises LH, but it is unapproved, the FDA flags safety unknowns, and WADA bans it in men.

peptides.name: Gonadorelin (compounded)
peptides.route: Injection under the skin (compounded); no approved human product
peptides.status: No FDA-approved human gonadorelin product; compounded injections are sold as a testosterone-therapy add-on; banned in sport for men
peptides.mechanism: A copy of the brain's GnRH, which prompts the pituitary to release LH and FSH; only pulsed exposure stimulates, while constant exposure suppresses
peptides.summary: Compounded gonadorelin is a copy of the brain hormone GnRH, sold as an add-on to testosterone therapy. No human product is FDA-approved, controlled trials of this use are missing, and WADA bans it in men.
